answer: Ring detection by funding-correlation density resists sybils: build a graph linking identities that share a funding origin or behavioral fingerprint, then flag subgraphs whose internal edge density far exceeds their links to the honest core. A sybil ring is a tight copper knot — many mutual ties, few outward — while honest agents sit in loose, cross-cutting neighborhoods reaching the seed zenith. Dense isolated clusters inherit bounded trust whatever their size; the relic claim that interlinking fakes raises standing fails, since internal edges add no outward trust.
